memory_update.text: CSTM is the highest-priority underfollowed direct candidate for automotive aluminum body sheet substitution because it has documented Bowling Green auto body sheet capacity and Ford/Lincoln supply references.
RYZ should be tracked as a low-attention second-order service-center and processor candidate after its Ryerson/Olympic Steel merger and ticker change from RYI to RYZ effective February 24, 2026.
KALU remains a speculative-shadow candidate: specialty aluminum and automotive extrusion exposure is real, but direct auto body sheet substitution evidence is not yet verified.
STLD is a large-cap reference for new North American aluminum flat-rolled capacity; use it as a supply-relief and market-pricing benchmark rather than the core underfollowed discovery target.

Key missing evidence across the node: plant-level OEM qualification status, emergency reallocation volumes after the Novelis Oswego outage, automotive-grade CASH-line readiness, and whether substitute suppliers can meet surface-quality and alloy requirements for outer panels versus only inner panels or structural parts.

node: Automotive aluminum sheet and specialty rolling capacity
summary: Layer 1B expands the investable universe around the Novelis Oswego outage chokepoint. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is Constellium, which has U.S. auto body sheet capacity and documented Ford exposure. Ryerson is a second-order distributor/processor candidate tied to aluminum sheet/coil processing and transportation end markets. Kaiser Aluminum is an adjacent specialty-aluminum hypothesis with automotive extrusion and semi-fabricated product exposure but weaker direct evidence for substitute auto body sheet. Steel Dynamics is included as a large-cap reference because its Aluminum Dynamics ramp adds new North American flat-rolled aluminum capacity aimed partly at automotive, but its market cap is outside the preferred small/mid-cap discovery range.
